newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end off as bond yield flirts with 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end off as bond yield flirts with 7 pct.

text.p: U.S. stocks slumped as the long bond yield flirted with the key seven percent level, but volume was one of the slowest for 1996, despite a battery of announced merger deals.

"The bond market is really the story of the stock market. As rates go up, stocks are looking more and more expensive. The whole mindset of bonds has changed 180 degrees in the past week. There are fears of higher rates and that the Fed will raise rates sooner or later," said Oppenheimer's Michael Metz.
The Dow industrials lost 29 points to about 5694.
After Friday's 1-3/32 point drop, the long bond lost 15/32 in late trading to yield 6.99 percent. The last time the bond yield closed above seven percent was July 30 at 7.04 percent.

Treasuries were hit on Friday by very strong July durable goods orders and minutes from the FOMC's July 2-3 meeting that aggravated fears of a near-term rate hike. Analysts said bond prices were further weighed in thin Monday trading by upcoming supply. Treasury will sell $18.75 billion two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion five-year notes on Wednesday.
NYSE volume of about 281.41 million just edged past July 29's 281.35 million, the slowest full session so far this year.
Phil Roth, Dean Witter Reynolds' chief technical analyst, noted: "August tends to be the lightest month of the year and the last week of August tends to be one of the lightest."
Losers outpaced gainers 13-8 on the NYSE.
The Nasdaq Composite lost four to about 1139.

Metz, Oppenheimer's chief investment strategist, said the flurry of merger pacts announced this morning "was the only place with any real upside action and Philip Morris." Morris and tobacco shares recouped some of their stiff losses after an Indiana jury ruled late on Friday in favor of major U.S. tobacco companies in a tobacco liability case.
Morris was the most-active NYSE issue and rose 2-1/4 to 90-1/4. R.J. Reynolds parent RJR Nabisco rose 1-1/8 to 26-1/2.

Among the deals announced, WorldCom Inc, off 3-5/8 to 22-3/4, agreed to merge with MFS Communications, up 9-15/16 to 44-13/16 in a stock swap worth at least $14 billion. The merger would provide a single source for a full range of local, long distance, Internet and international service over an advanced fiber optic network. Local telephone providers that rose amid hopes of further consolidation included Teleport Communications, up 1-3/8 to 23-5/8, McLeod, up 1-3/4 to 32-1/4 and Winstar, up 1-9/16 to 20-5/8.

Conseco rose two to 44 after news it would acquire two insurers and increase its stake in two others, giving it full ownership of those firms. Conseco agreed to buy American Travellers, up 3-3/16 to 31-9/16, for about $793 million in Conseco stock and Capitol American Financial, up 9-7/8 to 34-7/8, for about $650 million in cash and Conseco stock.

Silver King Communications, off 1-1/2 to 28, agreed to acquire Home Shopping Network, up 1/8 to 11-3/8 in exchange for stock. The proposed merger would reunify the two companies which split in 1992 and supercedes a previous pact to purchase only Liberty Media's controlling interest in Home Shopping.
AccuStaff Inc, off three to 25, and Career Horizons definitively agreed to merge in a stock deal valued at an estimated $1 billion. Career Horizons jumped 5-1/8 to 37.
Chancellor Broadcasting agreed to buy 12 radio stations from Colfax Communications for $365 million in cash and working capital. Chancellor rose 1/4 to 37-1/2.
Columbus McKinnon, off 3/4 to 14, reached a definitive agreement to acquire Spreckels Industries for $24 a share. Spreckels climbed 4-1/8 to 23-1/2.
Advanced Medical, up 7/16 to 2-7/8, agreed to buy IVAC Medical Systems in a cash deal valued at about $400 million.

Olympic Financial soared 6-1/4 to 23-7/8 after news it had hired Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette to examine strategic alternatives, said a possible acquirer had indicated interest in buying the company and said its chairman and chief executive was terminated.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.83 to 1139.22.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.15 to 663.88.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
